maya: Heads up — noticed the sampleapp demo created duplicate DB rows when we hit a token refresh + 429 surge. Repro steps in staging.

devon: ugh. is that the SDK retrying without an idempotency key? :grimacing:

maya: yeah. sampleapp uses the simple POST /generate flow, nothing sets Idempotency-Key. Sequence: auth refresh triggered, client retried, server returned 429 for a subset, then client replayed the request after backoff and it resulted in duplicate side-effects.

liam: do we have a standard guidance in SDKs for auto-inserting Idempotency-Key for mutating endpoints? iirc we avoided doing it automatically due to caching and token rotation concerns.

amanda: we recommended app-layer idempotency keys in docs, but onboarding/sampleapps should show the pattern. newbie DX is poor here.

devon: agree. quick mitigation: add jitter to the refresh-backoff and ensure SDK doesn't retry POSTs blindly when a refresh happened within last Xs. Also surface an opt-in auto-idempotency header for user apps that prefer convenience.

maya: repro snippet:
```
# client: node sampleapp
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <shortlived>
body: { prompt: "create invoice" }
```
If token rotation occurs mid-flow the client retried the whole request.

liam: what if we add an SDK config: {
  safeReplay: true | false,
  safeReplayWindow: 2000  # ms
}
When safeReplay is true, SDK auto-inserts X-Redwood-Req-Id and dedupes replays within window.

amanda: +1 for opt-in. default false for parity. But onboarding sampleapp should show how to set it and why.

devon: for 429s specifically we should ensure backoff uses full jitter and caps bulk retries across multiple concurrent clients. Observed stampeding: same client instance spun N parallel requests during onboarding load test.

ops-bot: Incident note: staging-db had 38 duplicates from sampleapp test at 2026-03-15T19:12:22Z. Cleared by QA.

liam: also add SDK telemetry flag when safeReplay is on so customers can see dedupe hits/misses in Console — helps evaluate risk.

maya: another edge: clock skew between client and server made dedupe window tricky for some server-side heuristics. We should prefer server-side monotonic dedupe key TTL anchored to request arrival time.

devon: implementation plan proposal:
- update node + python SDKs with opt-in safeReplay + X-Redwood-Req-Id header
- sampleapp: enable safeReplay by default and document tradeoffs
- docs: cookbook for idempotency patterns and token-rotation pitfalls
- console: add telemetry for dedupe stats

amanda: can someone create a small PR to update sampleapp and a short doc blurb? I'll add to onboarding checklist.

liam: I'll sketch the header behavior and a short test harness for race conditions.

devon: i'll add jitter tuning defaults: base=100ms, cap=2s, jitter=full. Also add a guard that avoids retry-if-token-rotated-within=500ms.

maya: thanks — that should reduce the noisy duplicates. :thumbsup:

amanda: filing follow-ups: #1 sampleapp PR, #2 docs blurb, #3 SDK opt-in implementation, #4 console telemetry. tagging owners.
